clue.text: Someone crawling underneath tobacco plant

indicators.note: in a down entry, being underneath means coming lower in the column, so this part is written second

parts.note: Virginia is a classic type of tobacco, named after the American state
one who creeps along

explanation.surface: A person slithers about below a growing tobacco plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tobacco plant' reads as one phrase, but the clue splits after tobacco: plant alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia creeper is a climbing vine with leaves that turn red in autumn, often grown over walls.

clue.text: Dispute after inferior article sold illicitly

indicators.note: says the first-named word follows the pair named after it in the finished answer

parts.note: lower in rank, as in an under-manager
the definite article
to counter an argument is to dispute it

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over some shoddy goods that were sold on the black market.
explanation.walkthrough: UNDER THE COUNTER: goods sold this way are passed over secretly rather than displayed openly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes trade conducted secretly or illegally, with goods kept hidden from public view.

clue.text: Blondie remix disc'll go OK

indicators.note: a remix reworks an existing recording into a new version, so the following letters get rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A fan hopes a new remix of a track by the band Blondie will turn out fine.
explanation.walkthrough: Blondie looks like the pop band, given remix and disc; here it is a fair-haired girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldilocks is the golden-haired girl of the fairy tale, and the name is used for anyone with blonde hair.

clue.text: Coming down to earth in middle age

parts.note: earth as ground or soil
taken as written

indicators.note: points to the central letter of the following word only

parts.note: the central of the three letters

explanation.surface: Someone in their forties or fifties is finally being brought back to reality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming down to earth' reads as one idiom, but earth belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing is the act of coming down from the air onto the ground, as an aircraft does.

clue.text: London police force's about to make arrest

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police; the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: Scotland Yard officers are on the point of detaining a suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: Arrest here is not detaining a person but checking a flow, as in stemming bleeding.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to halt or check it, the same sense as arresting decline or bleeding.

clue.text: In Verona, doc laid out old artist

indicators.note: out here means disordered or awry, so the letters before it take a new order

parts.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: In the Italian city of Verona, a physician once laid out the body of an elderly painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid out' reads as one phrase, but laid belongs to the letters to rearrange and out alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci was the Italian Renaissance painter of the Mona Lisa, born in the fifteenth century.

clue.text: Perhaps cellist playing important part is German

parts.note: being instrumental in something is playing a key role in it
ist is the German word for is

explanation.surface: A German musician, maybe a cellist, takes a leading role in the performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is German' means the German for is, not a statement of nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellist is one example of a musician who plays an instrument, hence the hedge perhaps.

clue.text: Mixture of grapefruit and tangerine with lemon in a cocktail

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixed drink, so the letters named alongside are mixed up

parts.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A fruity drink: grapefruit, tangerine and a squeeze of lemon mixed together.
explanation.walkthrough: Mixture looks like the anagram signal but it belongs to the definition; cocktail does the mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: A minneola is a tangelo, a hybrid citrus fruit bred from a grapefruit or pomelo crossed with a tangerine.

clue.text: Couple with fashionable society connections

parts.note: to couple is to tie together
in fashion
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A pair with links into the smart set.
explanation.definitionFit: Tie-ins are links or associations between things, such as a book tied to a film release.

clue.text: Settled on a good instrument

parts.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation
a reed instrument such as an oboe; reed also names the instrument's vibrating part

explanation.surface: Someone chose a decent musical instrument after deliberation.
explanation.definitionFit: Parties who have agreed a matter have reached a decision on it together, so the point is fixed.

clue.text: I'm a noted spin master

indicators.note: spinning whirls things round, leaving the preceding letters in a fresh order

parts.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A boast from a famous political spin doctor or spin bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: To master an opponent or situation is to gain complete control over it, overpowering it.

clue.text: Insect bite seen from behind

indicators.note: viewing from the back means starting at the end, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a sharp taste, as in a cheese with some bite

explanation.surface: A sting noticed on someone's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Bite suggests an insect bite, but it means a sharp flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a small two-winged fly, some kinds of which bite people.

clue.text: Lou, Gus and Nora are confused and listless

indicators.note: confusion jumbles things, so the letters of the three names are scrambled

parts.note: the letters of the three names; and only joins them in the surface

explanation.surface: Three friends are muddled and lacking energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Languorous describes a lazy, dreamy lack of energy, just as listless means without spirit or vigour.

clue.text: Foolishly, Susan diets without any help

indicators.note: acting foolishly means acting in a muddled way, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Susan is unwisely trying to slim with no support from anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on your own, receiving no aid from others, is to do it alone and unhelped.

clue.text: Beat villain, then beheaded receiver of stolen goods

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter is cut off the word that follows

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man
slang for one who handles stolen property

explanation.surface: Someone defeats a crook and then decapitates a dealer in stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Beat looks like a verb for defeating the villain; it is a noun, the rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadence is the rhythm or rise and fall of sound, as in speech or music, so it means a beat.

clue.text: Chinese rulers closed German city

parts.note: the Han dynasty ruled China for four centuries
finished, ended

explanation.surface: Chinese leaders shut down a city in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanover, or Hannover, is a city in Lower Saxony, northern Germany, and gave its name to a British royal house.

clue.text: Cathedral cleric, not single

indicators.note: tells us to remove from the word for a cleric a letter meaning single

parts.note: a member of the clergy
the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A clergyman at the cathedral who happens to be married.
explanation.walkthrough: Single looks like marital status; it is the numeral I, taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: A minster is a large church, often an important one such as York Minster, and many are cathedrals.

clue.text: Transports turbulent popish sort

indicators.note: turbulence throws everything about, so the following letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A rowdy Catholic type is carried away with excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: Transports looks like a verb, as in delights; it is a plural noun for ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Troopships are vessels for carrying soldiers, and transports is the military noun for such carriers.

clue.text: A lot transposed for counter-tenor

indicators.note: transposing music or letters shifts their positions, giving a new order here

parts.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A lot of music shifted into a different key for a high male singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Transposed has its musical sense in the surface, fitting the singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A male alto sings in the same high range as a countertenor, so the two voice names are used interchangeably.

clue.text: Confused, state imprisons girl for illiberality

indicators.note: a prisoner is shut inside, so one word is placed within the other

parts.note: a confused state is a mess
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A muddled government locks up a young woman for intolerance.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits the phrase in the surface, but confused state together means a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Illiberality means stinginess or lack of generosity, and meanness is the everyday word for that quality.

clue.text: Tackle Tony about fee-paying school

indicators.note: the answer is found lying about inside the neighbouring words, spread across them

parts.note: letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone takes Tony to task over private school fees.
explanation.walkthrough: About usually signals a reversal, but here the letters read forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a famous English independent boarding school near Windsor, charging high fees.

clue.text: Makes silent pictures

definitions.meaning: second meaning: photographs from a film

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as making silent films, but it splits into a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To still a crowd is to hush it, and stills are single photographs taken from a film.

clue.text: Aesthete, romantic — but essentially not gay!

indicators.note: in essence means at the core, so the answer sits inside the words before it

parts.note: letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: An arty, romantic type turns out to be straight after all.
explanation.walkthrough: The aesthete suggests a camp stereotype, which the clue then wittily overturns.
explanation.definitionFit: Hetero is short for heterosexual, attracted to the opposite sex, hence not gay.

clue.text: Work out a couple of errors in VAT, perhaps

indicators.note: says those letters go inside the next word

parts.note: VAT is one example of an excise or duty

indicators.note: a couple means two, so we keep just the opening pair of letters

parts.note: the opening pair of letters

explanation.surface: Someone tries to calculate the mistakes in their sales-tax return.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is value added tax, Britain's sales tax; strictly excise is a duty on goods, but the 'perhaps' covers it.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise is to work out, as in physical training at the gym.
